cds.text: Identify how texts have different language features and are typically organised into characteristic stages by purpose
Describe how spoken, written and multimodal texts use language features and characteristic stages and phases
Explain how curriculum texts are organised into stages and phases by purpose, noting that authors adapt structures and features
Identify how connectives (temporal and conditional words) and topic word associations sequence and connect ideas
Understand how sentence or paragraph starting points give prominence to the message and guide the reader
Understand that cohesion can be created through intentional repetition and word associations
Identify online text navigation features that enhance readability, such as headlines, drop-down menus, links, graphics and layout
Plan, create, edit and publish texts with visual features, linked ideas, complex sentences, appropriate tense, synonyms, antonyms, correctly spelled multisyllabic words and simple punctuation
Plan, create, edit and publish texts with visual features, suitable structure, text connectives, expanded noun groups, specialist vocabulary and dialogue punctuation
Plan, create, edit and publish texts with paragraphs, varied complex sentences, expanded verb groups, tense, vivid vocabulary, punctuation, spelling and visual features
Plan, rehearse and deliver structured presentations to report, tell stories, recount events or argue, using subjective and objective language, complex sentences and visual features
Plan, rehearse and deliver presentations with elaborated, sequenced ideas, complex sentences, specialist vocabulary, delivery features and visual or digital features
Plan, rehearse and deliver presentations that develop a theme through arguments and details, using precise vocabulary, delivery features and visual or digital features
Write words using clearly formed joined letters, with developing fluency and automaticity

sentences.text: {{S}} experiments with narrative writing features, showcasing creativity and thoughtfulness.
{{S}} plans and structures informative and persuasive texts effectively and incorporates descriptive language to engage the reader.
{{S}} shows a strong understanding of how to plan, structure and revise persuasive texts.
{{S}} uses a variety of sentence structures and writes using past, present and future tenses to suit different text types.
{{S}} plans, drafts and revises persuasive texts effectively.
{{S}} applies a variety of tenses to suit different writing tasks.
{{S}} maintains a consistent point of view throughout imaginative writing.
{{S}} argues against opposing views to strengthen {{pos}} persuasive writing.
{{S}} backs up a clear main argument about a text with evidence from it.
{{S}} works with others to write texts that bring together different ideas and values.
{{S}} reflects on how planning and revising changes the clarity of {{pos}} writing.
